question:
A 6-year-old girl is brought to the physician for pain and increasing swelling over her scalp for 1 month. She has not had any trauma to the area. There is no family or personal history of serious illness. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a 3-cm solitary, tender mass over the right parietal bone. X-ray of the skull shows a solitary osteolytic lesion. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL
Leukocyte count 7300/mm3
Serum
Na+ 136 mEq/L
K+ 3.7 mEq/L
Cl- 103 mEq/L
Ca2+ 9.1 mg/dL
Glucose 71 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Solitary osteolytic lesion on X-ray -> Swelling and pain over the scalp -> 80% CHAIN: Hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL -> Suggests mild anemia -> 70% CHAIN: Leukocyte count 7300/mm3 -> Within normal limits -> 90% CHAIN: Serum electrolytes within normal limits -> No electrolyte imbalance -> 80% CHAIN: Glucose 71 mg/dL -> Normal blood glucose level -> 90% CHAIN: Most likely diagnosis: Ewing sarcoma -> 80%
analysis: The presentation of a solitary osteolytic lesion in the skull of a 6-year-old girl, along with the clinical symptoms of pain and swelling, is highly suggestive of a primary bone tumor. Among the options provided, Ewing sarcoma is the most likely diagnosis in this scenario. Ewing sarcoma commonly presents as a painful, rapidly growing mass in the bone, often affecting the long bones or pelvis. It is more common in children and adolescents, with a peak incidence in the second decade of life. The laboratory findings are not specific to Ewing sarcoma but can be within normal limits in many cases.
